output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs comes mainly from inside Brackenford, not from Haverlow. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, night pallets wait about 3 h 52 min on an unrefrigerated dock (15–17°C) instead of about 44 min. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier alike, while day-shift rates barely moved. Haverlow's trailer data shows loads at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open, and unloading took about 40 minutes. The warm probe readings were taken after the long dock wait, so they show warming on the dock, not warm arrivals. The chambers held temperature. I'm fairly confident (about 80%). Next step: drop the Haverlow chargeback and volume move, restore night receiving to six operatives, set a maximum dock-to-chamber time with weekly monitoring, and review the concessions given on warm loads. Keep the night temperature probe. Part of the rise in customer credits may come from Corriebank's easier self-certified claims. That is unproven, so request their claim-level data and check a sample before changing their terms.
